svg.text: no upstream build, distributions only; no optimizations

g.title: libpq - blue (critical) Release: Debian Gap: libpq is built in-tree with PostgreSQL (src/interfaces/libpq) and shares its riscv64 status entirely. The primary GitHub Actions pipeline (pg-ci.yml) has zero riscv64 references, but the PostgreSQL Build Farm -- the project's official distributed CI -- has 3 active riscv64 workers (boomslang, copperhead on Debian 13/gcc14; greenfly on Ubuntu 24.04/clang 22.1.6) that run the full regression suite on master and all supported stable branches ([Build Farm riscv64 members](https://buildfarm.postgresql.org/cgi-bin/show_members.pl?os=Linux&arch=riscv64)). PostgreSQL ships source-only tarballs; libpq5 riscv64 is available in Debian trixie, Ubuntu 24.04 Noble (ports), and Arch Linux RISC-V (18.4-1). The report cited 4 workers; a live check on 2026-08-27 shows mollusk has dropped off, leaving 3 active workers.

psycopg - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: The `packages-bin.yml` CI workflow (read live from psycopg/psycopg) includes `riscv64` in its full build matrix and executes `pytest {project}/tests` (with `-m 'not slow and not flakey'`) against a live PostgreSQL service under QEMU for every riscv64 arch/platform combination - this is not build-only CI. Upstream publishes 10 riscv64 binary wheels for psycopg_binary 3.3.4 on PyPI (confirmed live: manylinux_2_39 and musllinux_1_2, Python 3.10-3.14). The pure-Python `psycopg` package (py3-none-any) is architecture-independent. No optimization-purpose modifier applies; psycopg is a protocol adapter with no SIMD or architecture-specific code.

pgx - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: pgx is a pure-Go library with no assembly, no CGo, and no ISA-specific code; Step 0 applies. The live CI workflow ([ci.yml](https://github.com/jackc/pgx/blob/master/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) confirms only ubuntu-22.04 and windows-latest runners, with zero references to riscv64, arm64, QEMU, or cross-compilation -- but Step 0 explicitly waives the CI requirement for architecture-independent projects. pgx publishes no compiled binary releases; it is consumed as Go module source via `go get github.com/jackc/pgx/v5`, with upstream (jackc) as the sole publisher, satisfying the green release-provider prerequisite.

pgjdbc - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: pgjdbc is a pure-Java Type 4 JDBC driver with no native code, no JNI, and no architecture-specific bytecode; Step 0 applies. Live verification of [REL42.7.13](https://github.com/pgjdbc/pgjdbc/releases/tag/REL42.7.13) (published 2026-07-06) confirms only `postgresql-42.7.13.jar` and its PGP signature are published -- no platform-specific assets. A recursive tree search of the repository finds zero native library files (.so, .dll, .dylib, JNI). riscv64 support is inherited entirely from the JVM runtime.

MariaDB Connector/C - yellow (optional) Release: Ubuntu Gap: No riscv64 CI exists in the upstream workflow (confirmed live: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on branch `3.4` is 212 lines with zero riscv matches). Ubuntu noble ships `libmariadb3` for riscv64 via the ports archive (version `1:10.11.7-2ubuntu2`), built from the `mariadb` source package (MariaDB Server 10.11.x, which bundles the connector) with no riscv64-specific distro patches, qualifying for the clean-distro-build yellow floor. The one required build-system fix ([PR #295](https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-connector-c/pull/295)) is confirmed merged (`merged_at: 2026-02-09`) and shipped in upstream v3.4.9.

go-sql-driver/mysql - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: go-sql-driver/mysql is a pure-Go library with no CGo, no assembly, and no architecture-specific files, satisfying the Step 0 architecture-independent shortcut: it compiles and runs on linux/riscv64 by construction using any Go 1.24+ toolchain. Live inspection of [`.github/workflows/test.yml`](https://github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql/blob/master/.github/workflows/test.yml) confirms no riscv64 CI exists (runners are `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`, `windows-latest` only), but Step 0 makes CI irrelevant for a source-only Go module with no compiled artifacts. The project distributes exclusively as a Go module via upstream GitHub releases, satisfying the `release_provider: upstream` prerequisite for green.

MariaDB Connector/C - yellow (optional) Release: Ubuntu Gap: No riscv64 CI exists in the upstream workflow (confirmed live: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on branch `3.4` is 212 lines with zero riscv matches). Ubuntu noble ships `libmariadb3` for riscv64 via the ports archive (version `1:10.11.7-2ubuntu2`), built from the `mariadb` source package (MariaDB Server 10.11.x, which bundles the connector) with no riscv64-specific distro patches, qualifying for the clean-distro-build yellow floor. The one required build-system fix ([PR #295](https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-connector-c/pull/295)) is confirmed merged (`merged_at: 2026-02-09`) and shipped in upstream v3.4.9.

go-sql-driver/mysql - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: go-sql-driver/mysql is a pure-Go library with no CGo, no assembly, and no architecture-specific files, satisfying the Step 0 architecture-independent shortcut: it compiles and runs on linux/riscv64 by construction using any Go 1.24+ toolchain. Live inspection of [`.github/workflows/test.yml`](https://github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql/blob/master/.github/workflows/test.yml) confirms no riscv64 CI exists (runners are `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`, `windows-latest` only), but Step 0 makes CI irrelevant for a source-only Go module with no compiled artifacts. The project distributes exclusively as a Go module via upstream GitHub releases, satisfying the `release_provider: upstream` prerequisite for green.

hiredis - yellow (critical) Release: Debian Gap: Upstream CI (build.yml and test.yml) was read directly and confirmed: no riscv64 job exists in either file -- arm/aarch64 QEMU jobs with test execution are present but riscv64 is absent. Debian sid ships libhiredis1.1.0 1.2.0-6+b4 for riscv64 (confirmed "Installed" on buildd rv-osuosl-02); the +b4 suffix is a binNMU rebuild applied uniformly across all architectures, not a riscv64-specific patch, so the clean-distro-build yellow floor applies. hiredis is a Redis client library (protocol parsing + network I/O), not an optimization-purpose project, so the Step 2 modifier does not apply.

PostgreSQL - blue (critical) Release: Debian Gap: The PostgreSQL Build Farm (upstream-hosted at buildfarm.postgresql.org) has 3 active riscv64 workers (boomslang, copperhead, greenfly) running the full regression and tap test suite on master and all supported stable branches with no failures, confirmed live on [buildfarm.postgresql.org](https://buildfarm.postgresql.org/cgi-bin/show_members.pl?os=Linux&arch=riscv64). PostgreSQL ships source-only with no upstream binary releases for any architecture, so release provider is the distro. JIT is disabled on riscv64 in all distro packages due to LLVM segfaults, and Zbb/Zbc optimization patches (v4, Greg Burd) remain unmerged, but these are performance gaps only and do not affect the blue classification since PostgreSQL is not an optimization-purpose project under the color model.
MySQL - grey (critical) Release: none Gap: Data not available.

MariaDB - yellow (critical) Release: Debian Gap: MariaDB has zero upstream riscv64 CI confirmed by reading `.gitlab-ci.yml` (564 lines, zero riscv64 mentions) and all three GitHub Actions workflow files. Debian sid ships version 1:11.8.8-1 with build status "Installed" on native RISC-V builder `rv-osuosl-03`, and the [Debian patch series](https://salsa.debian.org/mariadb-team/mariadb-server/-/raw/HEAD/debian/patches/series) contains 17 patches with no riscv64-specific entries, qualifying for the yellow clean-distro-build floor. MDEV-29875 (RocksDB build failure) remains open but does not block the core InnoDB server build; the InnoDB sv39 fix (MDEV-39142, PR #4852) was confirmed merged 2026-03-25.

Redis - yellow (critical) Release: debian Gap: All 11 GitHub Actions workflow files (including 2 new ones not present in the June 2026 report: modules-build-flow.yml and post-release-automation.yml) contain zero riscv64 references, confirmed live 2026-08-27 via gh api. Debian sid ships redis 8.0.6-2 built on rv-osuosl-03 (status "Installed") from unpatched upstream source - the 6 Debian patches include only a kFreeBSD fix, build-flag additions, a jemalloc flag, and a CVE fix, none architecture-specific. PRs #15204 (Zbb popcount) and #15273 (HyperLogLog RVV) remain open and unmerged.

Valkey - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: No riscv64 CI exists in any Valkey workflow file (ci.yml, daily.yml with arm and s390x jobs, weekly.yml) and GitHub releases ship no binary artifacts for any architecture. Debian sid packages valkey 9.1.1-1 with [autopkgtest passing on riscv64](https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/valkey); the [Debian packaging carries only generic patches](https://sources.debian.org/src/valkey/9.1.1-1/debian/patches/) (kFreeBSD, CPPFLAGS, PATH_MAX, jemalloc, TLS tests) with no riscv64-specific patches, confirming a clean build from unmodified upstream source and qualifying for the yellow clean-distro-build floor.

KeyDB - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: The [ci.yml](https://github.com/Snapchat/KeyDB/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) workflow contains exactly four jobs (test-ubuntu-latest, build-ubuntu-old, build-macos-latest, build-libc-malloc), all targeting x86-64; the string "riscv" is absent, and there is no QEMU step or architecture matrix -- confirmed by live read of the file on 2026-08-27. No riscv64 binary or package exists in any channel: all GitHub releases (v6.3.2 through v6.3.4) have zero attached assets, and KeyDB is absent from Debian, Ubuntu 24.04, and Arch Linux RISC-V. The project builds on riscv64 via the generic POSIX path (one user report, [Issue #517](https://github.com/Snapchat/KeyDB/issues/517), Nov 2022), but this is a single anecdotal data point with no ongoing CI coverage or published artifact for the architecture.
Dragonfly - grey (optional) Release: none Gap: Data not available.

Memcached - yellow (critical) Release: Debian Gap: Upstream CI is a single 21-line GitHub Actions workflow targeting `ubuntu-latest` (x86_64) only -- confirmed by live read of [ci.yml](https://github.com/memcached/memcached/blob/master/.github/workflows/ci.yml). No riscv64 CI job exists anywhere in the repository. Debian sid ships memcached 1.6.45-1 with status "Installed" on riscv64 (buildd rv-osuosl-03) with no riscv64-specific patches, confirming a clean distro build ([Debian buildd](https://buildd.debian.org/status/package.php?p=memcached&suite=sid)). Yellow/clean-distro-build is the correct floor; note that Arch Linux RISC-V shows a test suite FTBFS at this version, indicating riscv64 test reliability issues outside Debian's environment.

pgvector - yellow (optional) Release: Ubuntu Gap: pgvector has no riscv64 CI ([build.yml](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/blob/master/.github/workflows/build.yml) confirmed: "riscv" appears nowhere), but Ubuntu 24.04 noble ships postgresql-16-pgvector (0.6.0-1) for riscv64 built from unmodified upstream source (PR [#948](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/pull/948) merged upstream 2026-01-14, the sole riscv64 change, confirms no distro patch is needed), qualifying for the yellow clean-distro-build floor. The optimization-purpose modifier does not apply: pgvector's primary value is the HNSW/IVFFlat ANN index algorithm and PostgreSQL integration, which remain fully functional on riscv64 via scalar C fallbacks -- scalar pgvector still far outperforms a brute-force SQL scan, so the project delivers its core value without RISC-V-specific optimizations.

PostGIS - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: PostGIS has zero upstream riscv64 CI: the live `.woodpecker/portability.yml` covers armhf, arm64v8, and s390x via QEMU but omits riscv64, confirmed by reading the file directly. Debian sid ships postgis 3.6.4+dfsg-2 for riscv64 with "Installed" status, and the Debian patch set (sfcgal-2.3.0.patch, relax-test-timing-constraints.patch, incorrect-path-for-interpreter.patch) contains no riscv64-specific patches, qualifying for the clean-distro-build yellow floor per the color model. PostGIS contains no architecture-specific code and is not an optimization-purpose project, so no downgrade modifier applies.

TimescaleDB - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: Debian builds and ships timescaledb 2.29.2+dfsg-1 on riscv64 with status "Installed" on buildd (rv-manda-04), confirmed via [buildd.debian.org](https://buildd.debian.org/status/package.php?p=timescaledb&suite=sid). The only Debian patch is [no-git-hook](https://salsa.debian.org/postgresql/timescaledb/-/raw/master/debian/patches/series), which removes a CMake git-hook installation step and is entirely architecture-neutral -- no riscv64-specific patches exist. This satisfies the clean-distro-build condition for yellow, upgrading from the proposed orange.

Apache AGE - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: All 5 upstream GitHub Actions workflows run exclusively on ubuntu-24.04/ubuntu-latest (x86_64) with no riscv64 matrix axis, confirmed by reading [installcheck.yaml](https://github.com/apache/age/blob/master/.github/workflows/installcheck.yaml) live. Upstream GitHub Releases publish source tarballs only (confirmed live). Debian packages postgresql-18-age for riscv64 from unmodified upstream source with zero architecture-specific patches, producing a verified ELF64 RISC-V shared object (documented in report via binary inspection on rv-osuosl-02); release is provided by Debian, not upstream.
Citus - grey (optional) Release: none Gap: Data not available.

Patroni - green (optional) Release: upstream Gap: Patroni is pure Python with no compiled extensions; the live PyPI check for v4.1.5 returns exactly one wheel, `patroni-4.1.5-py3-none-any.whl`, published directly by upstream. Step 0 applies: architecture-independent, inherits riscv64 from CPython. The `.github/workflows/tests.yaml` contains zero references to "riscv" (verified live against master), confirming no riscv64 CI exists and none is needed -- the color requires only that the upstream artifact be architecture-neutral, which it is.

PgBouncer - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: Live inspection of [pgbouncer-ci.yml](https://github.com/pgbouncer/pgbouncer/blob/main/.github/workflows/pgbouncer-ci.yml) on 2026-08-27 confirms zero riscv64 references -- runners are ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-15, and windows-2022 only. Debian sid ships pgbouncer 1.25.2-1 built from unpatched upstream source on host rv-osuosl-01 with status "Installed" ([Debian buildd](https://buildd.debian.org/status/package.php?p=pgbouncer&suite=sid)), qualifying for the yellow clean-distro-build floor. PgBouncer is a network proxy daemon (connection pooling), not an optimization-purpose project, so the optimization modifier does not apply.

Pgpool-II - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: Pgpool-II has zero upstream CI for any architecture: `gh api repos/pgpool/pgpool2/contents/.github` returns HTTP 404, confirming no `.github/workflows` directory exists. The only Debian patch (`pgpool2-debian-config.patch`, 2016) adjusts default socket and pid-file paths -- a generic Debian packaging convention with no riscv64-specific content -- satisfying the clean-distro-build floor. Both [Debian sid](https://buildd.debian.org/status/package.php?p=pgpool2&suite=sid) and [Ubuntu 24.04 Noble](https://packages.ubuntu.com/noble/pgpool2) ship riscv64 binary packages from unpatched upstream source, confirming yellow (clean-distro-build).
pgcat - grey (optional) Release: none Gap: Data not available.

Vitess - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: A GitHub code search across the entire vitessio/vitess repository returns zero "riscv64" hits, confirming no CI job, no build matrix entry, and no conditional code targets riscv64 in any of the 46 workflow files ([workflows directory](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/tree/main/.github/workflows)). The [v24.0.2 release](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/releases/tag/v24.0.2) publishes only amd64 artifacts (tar.gz, x86_64 RPM, amd64 DEB); no riscv64 binaries or Docker images are present. No Vitess package was found in Ubuntu noble, Debian, or Arch Linux RISC-V, so no distribution floor applies; the project lands at plain orange with no evidence of riscv64 buildability from any source.
ProxySQL - grey (optional) Release: none Gap: Data not available.

RocksDB - orange (optional) Release: Debian Gap: Zero riscv64 CI jobs exist across all 14 GitHub Actions workflow files (live-confirmed 2026-08-27: zero matches for "riscv" in pr-jobs.yml and nightly.yml). Debian sid ships rocksdb 9.11.2-1 with a successful riscv64 build (host rv-manda-01, status "Installed"), but the packaging includes riscv64-relevant patches: patch `0001-replace-old-sync-with-new-atomic-builtin-equivalents.patch` explicitly cites riscv32/newer arches as the motivation for replacing `__sync_*` builtins, and `Extend-MIPS-adaptations-to-apply-to-all-remaining-archite.patch` extends MIPS timer fallbacks to all remaining architectures including riscv64; vanilla upstream source thus does not build cleanly without these fixes, placing the floor at orange (downstream-only). Key unmerged fixes (CMake riscv64 support, `-march` typo fix, LLD detection) remain stalled in open [PR #14530](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/pull/14530), last updated 2026-08-08 with no maintainer response.

MyRocks - orange (optional) Release: Debian Gap: facebook/mysql-5.6 has no riscv64 CI and was archived 2026-03-01, making upstream enablement impossible. MDEV-29875 (open, critical since 2022, last updated 2026-06-02) documents that MariaDB's RocksDB plugin requires Debian-carried patches to build on riscv64; the distribution floor for a patched build is orange not yellow. Debian sid ships [mariadb-plugin-rocksdb 11.8.8-1](https://packages.debian.org/sid/riscv64/mariadb-plugin-rocksdb) and Ubuntu 24.04 noble ships [10.11.7-2ubuntu2](https://packages.ubuntu.com/noble/riscv64/mariadb-plugin-rocksdb) as the only functional paths.

MariaDB ColumnStore - red (optional) Release: none Gap: Three independent riscv64 blockers are confirmed live on the develop branch as of 2026-08-27: (1) [CMakeLists.txt in MariaDB/server](https://github.com/MariaDB/server/blob/main/storage/columnstore/CMakeLists.txt) silently skips the entire ColumnStore build when `CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR` is not x86_64, amd64, or aarch64; (2) [mcs_int128.h](https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-columnstore-engine/blob/develop/datatypes/mcs_int128.h) has no `__riscv` guard so GCC falls through to the x86 SSE `movups` inline asm path, causing an assembler error; (3) [archcheck.h](https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-columnstore-engine/blob/develop/primitives/primproc/archcheck.h) returns UNKNOWN for riscv64 and [primproc.cpp line 711](https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-columnstore-engine/blob/develop/primitives/primproc/primproc.cpp) hard-aborts with "Unsupported CPU architecture. ARM Advanced SIMD or x86_64 SSE4.2 required; aborting." -- zero riscv64 issues or PRs exist and no distro packages are available.

Galera Cluster - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: Upstream CI (.travis.yml: Ubuntu Bionic x86-only; Jenkins; no GitHub Actions) targets only x86 with no riscv64 jobs. Debian sid builds galera-4 26.4.27-1 successfully on riscv64 (rv-manda-02, confirmed live 2026-08-27 via [Debian buildd](https://buildd.debian.org/status/logs.php?pkg=galera-4&arch=riscv64)); live check of [debian/rules](https://salsa.debian.org/mariadb-team/galera-4/-/raw/master/debian/rules) confirms `CK_TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER=5` is a global unconditional export ("make slow tests pass on loaded builders"), not a riscv64-specific patch -- clean distro build with no architecture-specific patches, confirming yellow and not orange.

MaxScale - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: MaxScale has no public CI of any kind: the [`.github/` directory](https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/MaxScale/tree/24.02/.github) contains only `dependabot.yml` with no `workflows/` subdirectory, confirmed by live GitHub API check on 2026-08-27. It is not packaged for riscv64 in Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, or Arch RISC-V, so the distribution floor does not elevate the grade. The source is BSL-licensed and buildable from source on riscv64 with workarounds for `install_cmake.sh` and `install_npm.sh`, but no upstream validation exists and no riscv64 release artifact is published by any provider.

RediSearch - red (optional) Release: none Gap: The primary integration path for Redis Stack (redis/redis `modules/Makefile`, `install-rust` target) contains an explicit `*) echo "Unsupported architecture"; exit 1` case that hard-fails for any architecture other than x86_64 and aarch64, including riscv64 -- confirmed live on the `unstable` branch at [redis/redis modules/Makefile](https://github.com/redis/redis/blob/unstable/modules/Makefile). The standalone RediSearch 2.x codebase has zero riscv64 CI across all 59 workflow files, no upstream releases for any architecture, and no distro package of the current 2.x series on riscv64 (Ubuntu 24.04 ships only the 7-year-old v1.2.2). No upstream-supported path to build or run RediSearch 2.x on riscv64 exists.

RedisJSON - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: The proposed "red" classification rested entirely on a `bindgen 0.22.1` pin, but a live check of the current `Cargo.lock` (HEAD as of 2026-08-27) shows `bindgen = 0.66.1`, well above the 0.60.0 release that fixed riscv64gc triple recognition; `redismodule-rs` tag v2.1.3 itself specifies `bindgen = "0.72.1"`. The specific build blocker from [Issue #830](https://github.com/RedisJSON/RedisJSON/issues/830) has been silently resolved through dependency updates, making the project likely buildable from vanilla upstream source. No riscv64 CI exists (flow-linux.yml accepts only x64/arm64, zero riscv64 mentions), no riscv64 binary is released, and no Linux distribution packages it for riscv64 -- qualifying for plain orange (no upstream CI, untested but not confirmed broken).

RedisBloom - red (optional) Release: none Gap: The [Makefile](https://github.com/RedisBloom/RedisBloom/blob/master/Makefile) contains an explicit `$(error ...)` call that hard-blocks any build on riscv64 by design (`$(error RedisBloom only supports 64-bit architectures (x64, arm64v8). Current architecture: $(ARCH))`), satisfying the red criterion of "explicit upstream statements that the architecture is unsupported." The proposed orange/downstream-only classification is wrong on two counts: no Linux distribution packages RedisBloom for riscv64 (Debian 404, Ubuntu noble absent, Arch RISC-V absent), so the downstream-only sub-type has no factual basis; and a deliberate build-system hard error -- confirmed live against the master branch pushed 2026-08-27 -- is confirmed breakage, not merely missing CI.

RedisTimeSeries - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: The [Makefile](https://github.com/RedisTimeSeries/RedisTimeSeries/blob/master/Makefile) contains a hard `$(error)` that explicitly blocks any build on architectures other than x64 and arm64v8, confirmed live on 2026-08-27 against the current master branch (last pushed 2026-08-25). No riscv64 CI exists across all 18 workflow files, no riscv64 binaries are released, and no Linux distribution (Ubuntu, Debian, Arch RISC-V) packages this module for riscv64 -- meaning the `color_case: downstream-only` in the proposed classification is incorrect (no distro ships it, so the distribution floor was never applied). Orange with no sub-type is correct: the project is actively blocked at build time with no upstream CI and no distro fallback.

mcrouter - red (optional) Release: none Gap: [`mcrouter/lib/Clocks.cpp`](https://github.com/facebook/mcrouter/blob/main/mcrouter/lib/Clocks.cpp) contains an unconditional `#error Unsupported CPU` in its `#else` branch with no `#elif defined(__riscv)` guard, confirmed by live fetch on 2026-08-27 -- riscv64 hits a compile-time failure before any binary can be produced. The hard dependency folly also has two open riscv64 build failures ([#2493](https://github.com/facebook/folly/issues/2493), [#2416](https://github.com/facebook/folly/issues/2416)) confirmed still open on 2026-08-27, compounding the blocker. No riscv64 CI, no distro packaging, and no RISE engagement exist for this project.

CloudNativePG - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: The [release-publish.yml](https://github.com/cloudnative-pg/cloudnative-pg/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-publish.yml) hardcodes `platforms="linux/amd64,linux/arm64"` with no riscv64 entry, confirmed live. The [v1.30.0 release assets](https://github.com/cloudnative-pg/cloudnative-pg/releases/tag/v1.30.0) contain linux binaries for arm64, ppc64le, s390x, and x86_64 but no riscv64 binary or container image manifest. Critically, the proposed `color_case: downstream-only` is wrong: no downstream distro (Ubuntu, Debian, Arch, Fedora) ships a CloudNativePG package at all -- this Kubernetes operator is distributed exclusively as a container image, and no riscv64 container image exists at any tier. The color remains orange (no CI, no artifacts) but with an empty color_case since neither `downstream-only` (requires a distro to ship it) nor `optimization-absent` (requires an optimization-purpose project) applies.

Zalando postgres-operator - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: The [publish_ghcr_image.yaml](https://github.com/zalando/postgres-operator/blob/master/.github/workflows/publish_ghcr_image.yaml) workflow explicitly lists `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64` for all four image builds (operator, pooler, UI, logical-backup) with no riscv64 entry. No distro package exists in Ubuntu Noble, no riscv64 assets appear in GitHub releases (v2.0.2 has 0 assets), and zero riscv64 issues or code references exist in the repository. Orange is confirmed; color_case "downstream-only" is a slight overstatement since no distro ships it, but no better sub-type exists for plain absent-CI with no distribution floor.

Percona Operator for MySQL - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: The [scan.yml CI workflow](https://github.com/percona/percona-server-mysql-operator/blob/main/.github/workflows/scan.yml) builds only `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`; no riscv64 job exists in any workflow (scan.yml, tests.yml, reviewdog.yml). No riscv64 container image is published (GitHub releases v1.0.0-v1.2.0 all have zero binary assets). The distribution floor does not apply because this operator has no Debian/Ubuntu/Arch package -- it is distributed exclusively as container images.

postgres_exporter - yellow (optional) Release: upstream Gap: The CI workflow [ci.yml](https://github.com/prometheus-community/postgres_exporter/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) delegates all cross-compilation to the [promci/build composite action](https://github.com/prometheus/promci/blob/main/build/action.yml), which runs only `promu crossbuild` with no test step; all tests (`test_go` job) run exclusively on `ubuntu-latest` (x86_64). Upstream publishes `postgres_exporter-0.20.1.linux-riscv64.tar.gz` on the GitHub releases page, confirming riscv64 build-only CI with a released artifact but no test execution on riscv64, which caps the grade at yellow.

MySQL Operator for Kubernetes - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: No riscv64 CI exists (`.github/workflows` returns HTTP 404, confirmed live; both Jenkinsfiles have 0 riscv64 references). The `build.sh` script rejects riscv64 with `exit 1` via a `^(amd64|arm64)$` guard, confirmed live against current HEAD `fd5c6bcf` (2026-07-21). No distro packages the operator for riscv64, and the hard deployment blocker is the absence of Oracle-published MySQL Shell riscv64 RPMs required inside the container image. See [build.sh](https://github.com/mysql/mysql-operator/blob/trunk/build.sh) and [reports/oracle-mysql-op.md](reports/oracle-mysql-op.md) Section 7-8.

mysqld_exporter - yellow (optional) Release: upstream Gap: Upstream cross-compiles and ships `mysqld_exporter-0.20.0.linux-riscv64.tar.gz` via the promu toolchain for every release, confirmed in the [v0.20.0 release assets](https://github.com/prometheus/mysqld_exporter/releases/tag/v0.20.0). All CI workflow files (`ci.yml`, `integration.yml`) run exclusively on `ubuntu-latest` (x86_64); the `build` job cross-compiles the riscv64 binary but neither `test_go` nor `integration` executes any test suite on riscv64 -- no QEMU, no riscv64 runner, no architecture matrix anywhere. Yellow/build-only-ci is the correct and confirmed grade; the optimization modifier does not apply to an observability tool.

mariadb-operator - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: The operator is pure Go (CGO_ENABLED=0) with zero architecture-specific source code, but a compiled Go binary is still an architecture-specific artifact -- Step 0 does not apply. No riscv64 CI exists of any kind and no Linux distribution (Debian, Ubuntu, Arch RISC-V) packages the operator for riscv64, so neither the downstream-only nor the clean-distro-build floor applies; the base orange case stands.

mysqld_exporter - yellow (optional) Release: upstream Gap: Upstream cross-compiles and ships `mysqld_exporter-0.20.0.linux-riscv64.tar.gz` via the promu toolchain for every release, confirmed in the [v0.20.0 release assets](https://github.com/prometheus/mysqld_exporter/releases/tag/v0.20.0). redis_exporter - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: No upstream riscv64 CI exists in any of the five workflow files (verified live against release.yml and tests.yml on 2026-08-27), and the latest release v1.90.0 ships 9 Linux binary tarballs (386, amd64, arm, arm64, mips64, mips64le, ppc64, ppc64le, s390x) with riscv64 absent. The Makefile build-all-binaries target and Docker platform string (linux/amd64,linux/arm,linux/arm64) also omit riscv64. No distro (Debian, Ubuntu, Arch RISC-V) packages the project, so the distribution floor does not apply. The project is pure Go with CGO_ENABLED=0 and builds correctly from source, but no pre-built artifact is available from any channel. See [release v1.90.0 assets](https://github.com/oliver006/redis_exporter/releases/tag/v1.90.0) and [release.yml workflow](https://github.com/oliver006/redis_exporter/blob/master/.github/workflows/release.yml).

memcached_exporter - yellow (optional) Release: upstream Gap: The CI workflow at [.github/workflows/ci.yml](https://github.com/prometheus/memcached_exporter/blob/master/.github/workflows/ci.yml) has a `test_go` job that runs only on `ubuntu-latest` (x86_64) with a live Memcached container, and a `build` job that calls `prometheus/promci/build` to run `promu crossbuild` for all platforms including riscv64 - cross-compilation only, no test execution on riscv64. Upstream ships `memcached_exporter-0.17.0.linux-riscv64.tar.gz` as a first-class release asset confirmed via live check; yellow applies per the color table when CI builds but does not test riscv64 (release presence does not upgrade to green without passing test suite on riscv64). The project is pure Go with no architecture-specific code, so no optimization modifier applies.

Kubernetes - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: Live check of [hack/lib/golang.sh](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/hack/lib/golang.sh) on 2026-08-27 confirms zero occurrences of "riscv" anywhere in the file; all four `KUBE_SUPPORTED_*_PLATFORMS` arrays enumerate only `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`, `linux/s390x`, and `linux/ppc64le`. No commits to that file since the report date of 2026-06-17. A new open PR #141291 (2026-08-10, not merged) proposes adding riscv64 only to the pause image build -- it does not add riscv64 to the supported platform arrays and does not change the classification. Debian sid ships a patched (`+ds`) kubectl-only build with no server-side components; Arch RISC-V has community packages with uncertain patch status; neither constitutes a consumable upstream Kubernetes release, so `release_provider: none` stands.

containerd - yellow (optional) Release: upstream Gap: containerd nightly CI cross-compiles riscv64 from an x86_64 host (confirmed in [.github/workflows/nightly.yml](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/.github/workflows/nightly.yml)) but executes no test step; ci.yml contains zero riscv64 references. [PR #13124](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/13124), which would add RISE-runner-backed integration tests, remains open and unmerged as of 2026-08-08.

runc - yellow (optional) Release: upstream Gap: Upstream cross-compiles and ships `runc.riscv64` in every release (confirmed in [v1.5.1](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases/tag/v1.5.1), 2026-07-14 via `gh api`), but all four GitHub Actions workflow files (`test.yml`, `validate.yml`, `scheduled.yml`, `actionlint.yml`) contain zero riscv64 jobs -- the binary is never built or tested in CI before release. [Issue #5166](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/5166) requesting riscv64 CI was confirmed closed 2026-03-12 without resolution, matching the report; Ubuntu noble and Debian trixie/sid also ship riscv64 packages from unpatched source, providing an independent distribution floor confirming buildability.

etcd - orange (optional) Release: Debian Gap: etcd has zero upstream riscv64 CI (all CI runs on Kubernetes Prow, which has no riscv64 nodes; 12 GitHub Actions workflow files contain zero riscv64 references) and publishes no riscv64 release binaries -- confirmed live via [GitHub releases API](https://api.github.com/repos/etcd-io/etcd/releases) showing v3.7.1, v3.6.14, and v3.5.33 all have 8 assets with no riscv64 assets. Debian sid ships etcd for riscv64 but requires at minimum two riscv64-relevant patches: patch 0002 removes the os.Exit(1) startup gate that blocks riscv64 without ETCD_UNSUPPORTED_ARCH, and patch 0025 (`0025-Reduce-InitialMmapSize-on-32-bit-and-riscv64-archite.patch`, dated 2026-06-06) reduces InitialMmapSize from 10 GB to 16 MB specifically for riscv64 because "64-bit RISC-V buildds also seem to struggle" -- both confirmed in the [Debian patch series](https://salsa.debian.org/go-team/packages/etcd/-/raw/debian/sid/debian/patches/series); the patched distro floor is orange, not yellow.

Upstream publishes `helm-v4.2.4-linux-riscv64.tar.gz` on get.helm.sh (confirmed via GitHub release assets listing the .asc and .sha256.asc for that tarball), satisfying `release_provider: upstream`, but the absence of any riscv64 test execution caps the grade at yellow per the build-only-ci rule.

k3s - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: The orange classification is confirmed and strengthened: v1.36.4+k3s1 (2026-08-27) contains exactly 16 release assets covering only amd64, arm64, and armhf -- zero riscv64 assets -- per live check. The install script still calls `fatal "Unsupported architecture $ARCH"` on riscv64. No Linux distribution packages k3s for riscv64 (not Ubuntu, Debian, or Arch RISC-V), making the `downstream-only` color_case technically imprecise (that sub-type requires a distro to ship it), but orange is unambiguously correct since there is no upstream CI, no release artifact, and no distro package. A significant delta from the report: PR [#7778](https://github.com/k3s-io/k3s/pull/7778) (the primary enablement PR) is now **closed without merging** (state: closed, merged_at: null), worsening the outlook; draft CI PR [#13854](https://github.com/k3s-io/k3s/pull/13854) remains open with zero reviews.

Upstream ships source-only tarballs with no prebuilt riscv64 binaries; consumable riscv64 packages come from Debian, Ubuntu, and Arch Linux RISC-V, all from unpatched upstream source. OpenSSL is a security-first TLS library, not an optimization-purpose project, so the optimization cap in Step 2 does not apply, and blue is the correct and confirmed grade.

BoringSSL - yellow (optional) Release: none Gap: Two mandatory CQ-gated LUCI builders (`android_riscv64_compile_only` and `android_riscv64_prefixed_compile`) are present in [commit-queue.cfg](https://boringssl.googlesource.com/boringssl/+/refs/heads/main/infra/config/generated/commit-queue.cfg) without `includable_only`, and [cr-buildbucket.cfg](https://boringssl.googlesource.com/boringssl/+/refs/heads/main/infra/config/generated/cr-buildbucket.cfg) confirms both have `run_ssl_tests:false` and `run_unit_tests:false` - build-only cross-compilation on x86-64 hosts. BoringSSL is a security-first crypto library (not an optimization-purpose project), so the optimization-absent cap does not apply; yellow stands on build-only CI alone. No binary releases exist; the project is source-only with no riscv64 artifacts from any upstream, RISE, or distro channel (Debian ships only an Android fork variant).

zlib - blue (critical) Release: Ubuntu Gap: The OpenBSD/riscv64 job in [others.yml](https://github.com/madler/zlib/blob/develop/.github/workflows/others.yml) runs cmake configure, cmake build, AND `ctest --test-dir build` on riscv64 (QEMU via vmactions), confirming both build and test pass. Upstream ships source-only releases with no prebuilt binaries for any architecture; riscv64 binaries come from distros (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian sid, Arch RISC-V). The optimization-purpose modifier does not apply: zlib's primary value is DEFLATE correctness and RFC 1950/1951 compatibility, not raw speed -- scalar C on riscv64 fully delivers that value.
zlib-ng - grey (optional) Release: none Gap: Data not available.

LZ4 - yellow (critical) Release: Debian Gap: LZ4 upstream CI ([cross-platform.yml](https://github.com/lz4/lz4/blob/dev/.github/workflows/cross-platform.yml)) runs `make platformTest` on riscv64 under QEMU, which executes the full test suite -- so the primary grade is blue. However, LZ4 is an optimization-purpose library (speed is its sole value proposition) and the primary decompression hot path `LZ4_FAST_DEC_LOOP` is explicitly disabled on riscv64 (defined to 0 in lib/lz4.c lines 479-485) while enabled on x86 and aarch64; the only merged RISC-V code is a scalar Zicclsm unaligned-access optimization (PR #1648), placing the optimization level at minimal and capping the color from blue to yellow. Upstream ships no riscv64 binary -- only Windows executables and source tarballs -- so the consumable riscv64 release is provided by Debian/Ubuntu distro packages.

zstd - yellow (critical) Release: Ubuntu Gap: The RISC-V CI job in [dev-short-tests.yml](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/blob/dev/.github/workflows/dev-short-tests.yml) runs `make clean check` under QEMU (rv64gc baseline plus RVV vlen=128/256/512), which executes the full test suite -- confirmed via direct file read -- giving a blue primary grade. The optimization modifier caps to yellow (minimal level): RVV intrinsics are merged for row-hash match mask, ZSTD_copy16, and sequence conversion, but the three highest-impact paths remain in open unmerged PRs as of 2026-08-27: unaligned memory access (+74% compression on Zicclsm hardware, [PR #4596](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4596)), sequence decode fast path ([PR #4557](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4557)), and Huffman 4-way decompression ([PR #4622](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4622)). No upstream riscv64 binary release exists; the consumable riscv64 library is provided by Ubuntu 24.04 (v1.5.5) and Debian sid (v1.5.7).
snappy - grey (optional) Release: none Gap: Data not available.

jemalloc - orange (critical) Release: Debian Gap: Live inspection of [linux-ci.yml](https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc/blob/dev/.github/workflows/linux-ci.yml) confirms zero riscv64 runners, QEMU jobs, or cross-compile steps across all six workflow files; Debian sid ships libjemalloc2 5.3.1-2 for riscv64 from unpatched upstream source, providing the clean-distro-build yellow floor. However, jemalloc is an optimization-purpose allocator (named explicitly in the color model), and live inspection of configure.ac confirms riscv64 falls to the wildcard case with HAVE_CPU_SPINWAIT=0 -- no Zihintpause pause instruction, no RVV intrinsics, no RISC-V assembly anywhere -- so the absent-optimization modifier caps the grade from yellow to orange.

tcmalloc - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: tcmalloc has no riscv64 CI runner -- confirmed live in [ci/linux_docker_containers.sh](https://github.com/google/tcmalloc/blob/master/ci/linux_docker_containers.sh) (copyright 2026, only x86-64 and AArch64 containers defined). As an optimization-purpose allocator, its primary differentiator -- the per-CPU RSEQ slab -- is entirely absent on riscv64: [percpu.h](https://github.com/google/tcmalloc/blob/master/tcmalloc/internal/percpu.h) guards `TCMALLOC_PERCPU_RSEQ_SUPPORTED_PLATFORM` to x86_64 and aarch64 only, riscv64 gets RSEQ signature 0x0 (invalid sentinel) and falls back to the slower per-thread cache path; this absent optimization level caps the grade at orange.

PCRE2 - blue (critical) Release: Debian Gap: The `ptarmigan` job in [dev.yml](https://github.com/PCRE2Project/pcre2/blob/main/.github/workflows/dev.yml) runs both `ninja` (build) and `ctest -j$(nproc) --output-on-failure` (full test suite) inside a QEMU riscv64 container on every push to main/release branches, confirmed by live reading of the workflow file. Upstream ships source archives only with no riscv64 binary release; Debian sid (10.46-1+b2, built on rv-osuosl-01) and Ubuntu 24.04 provide the consumable riscv64 packages. The PCRE2-layer SIMD dispatch in `pcre2_jit_simd_inc.h` excludes `SLJIT_CONFIG_RISCV`, leaving character-scan fast-paths on scalar fallback, but PCRE2 is not an optimization-purpose project (its core value is correct regex matching, not throughput), so this gap does not cap the color below blue.

ICU - yellow (critical) Release: Debian Gap: ICU has no upstream riscv64 CI of any kind: the latest `icu4c.yml` (last changed 2026-08-03) contains zero riscv references, confirmed live. Debian sid ships ICU 78.3-2 built on hardware builder rv-manda-02 with status "Installed"; all 5 Debian patches (`32bit_selftest_fix.patch`, `do_not_hardlink_docs.patch`, `hurd-amd64.patch`, `icudata-stdlibs.patch`, `reverse_of_ICU-22610.patch`) are non-riscv64-specific, confirming a clean-distro-build. Step 2 optimization modifier does not apply: ICU is a Unicode correctness library with no hand-written SIMD for any architecture.

libevent - yellow (critical) Release: Debian Gap: No riscv64 CI exists in any of the four GitHub Actions workflow files - confirmed live against [build.yml](https://github.com/libevent/libevent/blob/master/.github/workflows/build.yml) on 2026-08-27, with zero matches for riscv64, qemu, or any non-x86 Linux target. Debian sid now ships libevent 2.1.13-stable-1 (upgraded from 2.1.12 since the report), built successfully on rv-manda-04 with no riscv64-specific patches, qualifying for the clean-distro-build yellow floor. libevent is pure portable C with no architecture-specific code, so the optimization-purpose modifier (Step 2) does not apply.

liburing - yellow (optional) Release: none Gap: The [CI workflow](https://github.com/axboe/liburing/blob/master/.github/workflows/ci.yml) contains a riscv64 matrix entry (`sanitize: 0`, `tsan: 0`) that cross-compiles the library and compiles a test program (`test_build.c`) against the installed library but never executes any binary -- the final step compiles `a.out` without running it. The latest release (liburing-2.15, 2026-06-29) has zero attached binary assets, confirming source-only upstream releases; riscv64 packages are provided by Debian sid and Arch Linux RISC-V from unpatched upstream source. liburing is a thin syscall wrapper with no SIMD or optimization-purpose code, so the Step 2 optimization modifier does not apply.

libnuma - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: All three upstream CI workflow files ([makefile.yml](https://github.com/numactl/numactl/blob/master/.github/workflows/makefile.yml), codeql.yml, cut-release.yml) run exclusively on ubuntu-latest (x86_64) with zero riscv64 references, confirmed by live read. Debian sid ships `libnuma1` 2.0.19-1+b2 built on native riscv64 hardware (`rv-osuosl-03`), status "Installed"; the Debian packaging `debian/patches/series` for 2.0.19-1 is empty (confirmed via Salsa GitLab API), meaning the package is built from completely unpatched upstream source. The clean-distro-build floor (yellow) applies; blue and green are unreachable without upstream riscv64 CI.

Protocol Buffers - yellow (optional) Release: Debian Gap: No riscv64 CI exists in any of the 26 upstream workflow files (confirmed by scanning all `.github/workflows/*.yml` files on 2026-08-27 with zero riscv hits and no riscv-related commits since 2026-06-17). Debian sid ships protobuf 3.21.12-16 with "Installed" status on riscv64 (rv-manda-03 buildd node); the full patch list at [sources.debian.org](https://sources.debian.org/patches/protobuf/3.21.12-16/) includes patches for hurd, s390x, x32, hppa, and loongarch64, but no riscv64-specific patch, confirming the package builds from vanilla upstream source and qualifies for the clean-distro-build yellow floor.

Lua - yellow (optional) Release: ubuntu Gap: Lua is pure ISO C99 with no architecture-specific code, assembly, or SIMD; confirmed by 404 on `.github/workflows/` (no CI for any architecture) and zero results from code search for `riscv`, `#ifdef __riscv`, or arch-specific files in [lua/lua](https://github.com/lua/lua). Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian sid both ship lua5.4 5.4.8-2 for riscv64 (Debian build "Installed" on rv-osuosl-05); the only Debian patches are `0001-build-system.patch` and `0002-lua-modules-paths.patch`, neither riscv64-specific, qualifying for the clean-distro-build yellow floor. Step 0 architecture-independent shortcut does not apply because Lua ships compiled binaries (lua, luac); Step 2 optimization modifier does not apply because Lua is a general-purpose runtime, not an optimization-purpose project.

xxHash - blue (optional) Release: none Gap: The `qemu-consistency` CI job in [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash/blob/dev/.github/workflows/ci.yml) cross-compiles for riscv64 and runs `make check` (the full test suite) under `qemu-riscv64-static` for both scalar and RVV (`XXH_VECTOR=XXH_RVV`) paths at vlen 128, 256, and 512 -- this is a genuine test-execution step, not build-only, confirming blue. The RVV backend in [`xxhash.h`](https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash/blob/dev/xxhash.h) covers all four primary XXH3 hot paths (`XXH3_accumulate_512_rvv`, `XXH3_accumulate_rvv`, `XXH3_scrambleAcc_rvv`, `XXH3_initCustomSecret_rvv`), yielding Full optimization coverage with no downward cap. The latest upstream release publishes only `xxhsum_win64_v0_8_3.zip`, so no riscv64 artifact is shipped upstream, keeping the grade at blue rather than green.

glibc - yellow (critical) Release: upstream Gap: The proposed "build-only-ci" justification is factually incorrect: live inspection of Buildbot build 525193 (builder 336, glibc-fedora-riscv) shows step 5 "make check" executing on a real riscv64 board (bpi-f3-2, BananaPi-F3) with result "test (failure)" -- tests ARE run on native hardware, but they fail. Both riscv64 Buildbot builders (293, 336) are now offline (0 workers confirmed via [Buildbot API](https://builder.sourceware.org/buildbot/api/v2/builders/293/workers); last build on 336 was June 2025). Yellow is still correct because no passing riscv64 test run exists in upstream CI, but the mechanism is "tests run and fail on native hardware" not "build-only." Distros (Debian, Ubuntu, Arch) ship glibc 2.44 for riscv64 from unpatched upstream source, confirming the yellow floor independently.

libmvec - orange (optional) Release: none Gap: libmvec does not exist for riscv64 in upstream glibc: `sysdeps/riscv/configure.ac` never sets `build_mathvec=yes`, so the library is not built for riscv64 in any released glibc version. No distro ships libmvec for riscv64 (confirmed across Debian, Ubuntu, Arch RISC-V, and Fedora per [reports/libmvec.md](reports/libmvec.md)). Live adversarial check of libc-alpha July and August 2026 archives confirms zero libmvec RISC-V submissions, validating the stall continues through 2026-08-27 per the [August 2026 libc-alpha index](https://sourceware.org/pipermail/libc-alpha/2026-August/).
